title: Drakengard 3
subtitle: A singer sets out to kill her sisters
summary: Drakengard 3 is Access Games' PlayStation 3 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 19 December 2013. Zero, an Intoner whose song carries magical power, travels with the dragon Mikhail to kill the five sisters ruling the world's regions. The campaign gradually changes the meaning of that apparent rampage, withholding the reasons behind her actions until the player has spent time within its violence and strange humour. Ground battles and dragon encounters continue the series' structure, while the central relationship brings an unexpectedly childish companion beside a protagonist whose behaviour is difficult to trust.
body: Drakengard 3 is Access Games' PlayStation 3 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 19 December 2013. Zero, an Intoner whose song carries magical power, travels with the dragon Mikhail to kill the five sisters ruling the world's regions. The campaign gradually changes the meaning of that apparent rampage, withholding the reasons behind her actions until the player has spent time within its violence and strange humour. Ground battles and dragon encounters continue the series' structure, while the central relationship brings an unexpectedly childish companion beside a protagonist whose behaviour is difficult to trust.

Zero attacks groups of enemies with several weapon types, each offering a different range and rhythm. Switching between them during combat allows the player to alter an approach without pausing the action. Successful attacks build the Tension Gauge, which enables a temporary Intoner state with greater speed, damage and protection. The player decides when that advantage is worth using, then returns to ordinary fighting once it ends. Dragon sections place Mikhail in the centre of another scale of encounter, connecting the series' ground-based violence to its aerial identity.

Yoko Taro returned alongside producer Takamasa Shiba and writer Sawako Natori, with Keisuke Mori also directing at Access Games. The score, led by Keiichi Okabe, connects the production to the team behind Nier while supporting a very different cast and tone. Western editions arrived in May 2014. Reviews welcomed parts of the story and ground combat while criticising technical performance and other elements. Drakengard 3 remains distinctive for the gap between the action first presented and the motives later revealed, asking the player to reconsider a journey already carried out.
